questions.q: Why does Business Critical have lower latency than General Purpose, per this lesson?
options: Business Critical's storage rides on local SSD attached to the compute node itself, while General Purpose's storage is remote
Business Critical uses the DTU purchasing model exclusively
Business Critical always runs on more vCores than General Purpose
There is no latency difference between the two tiers
questions.explain: Local SSD storage is physically closer to compute, which is also why Business Critical costs more per GB.

questions.q: Is scaling a database's compute or service tier truly zero-downtime?
options: No — it's near-zero-downtime; there's a brief reconnect window during cutover, so applications still need retry logic
Yes — it is always perfectly instantaneous with no interruption
No — scaling always requires taking the database fully offline for hours
Scaling is not possible without recreating the database from a backup
questions.explain: Azure creates a new copy at the target size and cuts over the connection, typically completing in minutes, but a brief reconnect window remains.

questions.q: Which service tiers support read scale-out, and why?
options: Business Critical and Hyperscale, because they already maintain a secondary replica as part of their built-in HA architecture
General Purpose only, because it's the cheapest tier
All three vCore tiers equally support read scale-out
Only the DTU model's Premium tier supports read scale-out
questions.explain: General Purpose doesn't maintain that kind of HA replica, so it has no secondary to route read-only connections to.

questions.q: What does enabling read scale-out actually change, per this lesson?
options: It gives read-heavy connections a secondary replica to go to, so they stop competing with transactional writes on the primary — it doesn't change what runs on the primary itself
It moves all write operations to the secondary replica
It permanently disables the primary replica
It requires provisioning and paying for an entirely new, separate database
questions.explain: It's a free capability on supporting tiers because the HA secondary already exists for HA reasons — no additional replica needs provisioning.

questions.q: In the example configuration this lesson walks through, why is Business Critical chosen as the service tier?
options: Because the workload needs read scale-out plus low latency, which General Purpose cannot provide
Because Business Critical is always the cheapest option available
Because Business Critical is required for any workload using the DTU model
Because Business Critical is the only tier that supports the Azure Portal
questions.explain: The example stacks purchasing model (vCore + Hybrid Benefit), service tier (Business Critical for read scale-out and latency), compute option, storage, and read scale-out into one coherent decision.
